findings.text: The elliptic section classifies test_tangent_compiles_within_three_primals[finite_part] as a device-qualified bound, saying the bound of three is 'met on the one device and missed on the other' (lines 56-59) and recommending that the compile rows be moved to a host where the ratio is stable, with 'no tangent change needed' (line 207). The node's own retained H200 full-file log contradicts the device-qualified framing: logs/h200-tangents.log (job 1296858, SOURCE_REVISION=d06fe116a, completed '11 failed, 39 passed' at 12:08) records FOUR further elliptic compile rows over the same bound of three on the H200 -- complete_pole 9.894, harmonic_root_moments 3.006, cn_pole_moment 10.372, sn_pole_moment 9.616. None of those four identifiers appears anywhere in the fragment. So the ratio bound is exceeded on both devices, by different rows, and a reader acting on the fragment would conclude the elliptic compile rows are safe to run on the H200, which is false for four of them.

Class E is labelled 'This is a product defect' for the H200 primal bit-difference at test_edge_term_tangents.py:257. The evidence does not exclude the alternative the fragment itself concedes at lines 190-194: the CPU arm never reached the assertion (it timed out at 300 s), so the only device evidence is a one-bit difference at one element of 52024 on the GPU, which is equally consistent with device-level floating-point reassociation. The label commits to a cause the measurement cannot separate; recording it as 'product defect suspected, device alternative open until the CPU arm reaches the assertion' would be supported by the evidence.

The H200 cells for test_tangent_compiles_within_bound[flux_line_moments] and [flux_and_moment_terms] read 'fails; reason not yet printed (see note)', and the closing note (lines 209-215) explains the reason was unmeasured because the node's wall closed first. That reason is printable and printed: logs/h200-tangents.log, which the manifest's own evidence_inputs list as a source, records 'Failed: Timeout (>300.0s) from pytest-timeout' for both rows at lines 163 and 211. The cells are stale against evidence the run retained, so a reader at this revision is told a value is unmeasured when it is measured.

The note quotes the H200 arm's progress line as '......F......F...FFF' and uses its trailing F letters to mark two specific cells as failing. The log records '......F......F...FFFFF' (h200-tangents.log:44, five trailing F letters over 22 rows). The quoted receipt has two fewer failures than the log it cites, so the evidence offered for which cells fail does not match the log.

The tests: line names <logs>/cpu-gate.log as the gate that ran, and that file does not exist in the run's logs directory. The CPU gate it describes was killed (cpu-numeric-rows.log ends EXIT=137) before completing either file, and the manifest's own retry_failures concedes that flux_line_moments' wall is unmeasured and its value read from the older base log. Promotion reads its gate receipt from this line, so the named receipt cannot be opened.

The scratch runner re-implements a capability the repository already owns rather than extending it: scripts/nova_lane/run.sh is the lane launcher that writes the revision/tree/command header, exports TMPDIR, sets PYTHONPATH, and unsets UV_NO_SYNC/UV_RUN_RECURSION_DEPTH, and scripts/nova_lane/standing_suite.sh already runs every test file in its own fresh pytest process with the heavy tail on the H200 rung. This is a third runner of the same shape.
